From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: POC environment & MAP - request for org setup, keys, and peering

Hi all — adding technical details so Pulseware can prep. Summary: VPC peering + API access flow.

VPC peering (AWS example):
- Pulseware provides VPC ID and CIDR (e.g., 10.50.0.0/16) and a contact email for the peer accept step.
- We'll create a peering request from Redwood VPC (redwood-prod-peering) and share the request ID.
- Pulseware must accept in their console and configure route tables and security groups to allow inbound on TCP 443 from Redwood subnets.
- Expected time: we can issue the request within 4 hours of receiving details; acceptance + routes usually 12–48 hours.

API keys & org setup:
- We will create an org entity for Pulseware (org id: pw-org-<short>) and two API keys scoped: ingestion.write and inference.query. Keys will be rotational — we can schedule a 90-day rotation or leave as manually rotated per your preference.
- For service accounts (recommended): provide the team email for a service account owner (we'll attach key rotation notifications).

IP allowlist: provide one of the following: single public IPs OR a CIDR. If you only have NAT egress, provide the NAT IPs. We'll add entries at org-level and route-level.

Attachments: vpc_peering_template.txt (txt)

Ping me with the VPC ID & contact and I will open the request.

Jonas
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Hi Emma, Mina — quick note from security side. We reviewed Pulseware's initial questionnaire and have two items to resolve before peering goes live:

1) KMS key policy: if Pulseware requires us to access any keys, we need to confirm acceptable access patterns. For the POC, we recommend client-side encryption for sensitive payloads; otherwise we'll provide a managed key with usage logs forwarded to your SOC contact.
2) SOC2 artifacts: attaching the section of our compliance pack that covers network segmentation and peering controls. Please tell us if you need any additional evidence (attestation, penetration report excerpts).

We can grant temporary elevated logging retention for the POC window (Dec 13–17) to help with debugging; let us know if you want that.

Attachment: pulseware_soc_section.pdf (pdf)

Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
